In #mathlib4 > Design for positive cones I proposed and discussed removing the existing docs#ConvexCone and renaming docs#PointedCone to ConvexCone. docs#PointedCone forces the cone to contain 0, while docs#ConvexCone does not. The rationale is that

  1. docs#ConvexCone is barely used for downstream things, with docs#PointedCone usually used instead. This is probably because the latter definition has access to the submodule API.
  2. docs#PointedCone is the more common definition of a "convex cone."
  3. "Pointed cone" commonly means something different to docs#PointedCone (it means what Mathlib calls a "salient convex/pointed cone").
  4. There is no rationale for the original design decision that anyone can remember.

I've made a draft PR #37050 showing what this refactor would look like. I haven't done deprecations / moves yet.

I've made a new thread for visibility.
(pinging @Martin Winter @Bjørn Solheim @Yaël Dillies from the other thread; sorry for the spam)

There is one place were I use the current ConvexCone: the relative interior of PointedCone is naturally such a ConvexCone. However, this is just tinkering and not substantial. In fact, I imagine that most concepts that can be defined for (the current) ConvexCone R M make also sense for general Set M (e.g. lineal, salient, ...).
I will remove references to docs#ConvexCone in favour of docs#PointedCone from leaf to root.
#37054 - remove duplicate proof of hyperplane separation (should happen anyway in my view)
#37053 - replace ConvexCone with PointedCone in the Riesz extension theorem
#37417 - deprecate ConvexCone.IsGenerating (should happen anyway) @Bjørn Solheim
